title: Yummy Tender Fried Indian Wheat Gulab Jamun
description: Crispy fried dumplings in a sweet and sticky syrup, typically served as a dessert. This recipe uses a paleo-friendly alternative to traditional wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Ghee or vegetable oil for frying

instructions: Combine ghee or vegetable oil, flour, milk powder, lemon juice, cardamom powder, and baking soda in a hot pot vessel and mix well.
Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and forms a smooth dough.
Knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Heat ghee or vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Divide the dough into small balls and flatten them slightly.
Fry the dumplings until they are golden brown, about 3-4 minutes on each side.
Drain the fried dumplings on paper towels.
Soak the fried dumplings in gulab syrup for at least 30 minutes.
Serve the gulab jamun hot, garnished with chopped pistachios or almonds if desired.
Note: Traditionally, gulab jamun is cooked in a robata grill, but a deep frying pan can be used as a substitute.
Note: The dough can also be refrigerated for up to 24 hours and cooked later.
